claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructured state.
The reported HfNbTiVAl10 heterostructure features multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A graph-based machine-learning model can use hierarchical-heterostructure descriptors and local atomic-environment features to predict mechanical properties.
The proposed model will predict Young's modulus of HfNbTiVAl10 more accurately than thermophysical-parameter calculations, CALPHAD, and conventional first-principles methods.
The proposed model will predict yield strength of HfNbTiVAl10 more accurately than thermophysical-parameter calculations, CALPHAD, and conventional first-principles methods.
The proposed model will predict toughness of HfNbTiVAl10 more accurately than thermophysical-parameter calculations, CALPHAD, and conventional first-principles methods.
The proposed graph-based model will be more computationally efficient than the named prior methods.
Higher accuracy depends on having sufficient representative training data from similar high-entropy alloys.
Graph-based models can capture complex structural and chemical relationships across multiple scales.
Capturing multiscale structural and chemical relationships enables efficient learning of structure-property correlations relevant to hierarchical high-entropy alloys.
The model will reduce prediction error for Young's modulus, yield strength, and toughness by at least 20–30% relative to the named prior methods.
The model will be at least 10 times faster than the named prior methods.
Model reliability will decrease when the training data contain insufficient examples of hierarchical heterostructures.
Model reliability will decrease when the input descriptors fail to capture mechanically relevant structural features.
Model performance may degrade for alloys containing structural motifs absent from the training data.
The quantitative accuracy gains depend on training-dataset quality and size.
Poorly defined hierarchical descriptors or limited training data may produce smaller accuracy and efficiency improvements than predicted.
A blinded prospective benchmark can compare predictions made by a model trained without HfNbTiVAl10 against tensile and fracture measurements and against the named baseline methods.
Failure to achieve both at least 20% lower prediction error and at least 10-fold greater computational speed would falsify the hypothesis.
